He claims that the incredibly light recoil of the low powered rifle gave him bruises and that the sound was "like firing a bazooka". He also claimed that he had PTSD for a few hours afterwards.

The guys name is Gersh Kuntzman and he recently wrote an article on his experience firing an AR-15. I use the term article loosely since it is more of a propaganda piece littered with falsehoods, and inaccuracies. Some of these are:

  • He says it "feels like a bazooka" which makes absolutely no sense because a bazooka has no recoil and I highly doubt he's ever fired one.
  • He calls it an "assault weapon" which is silly since that is not an actual definition of anything.
  • He calls it a "machine gun" which is simply not the case, all AR-15s are semi automatic.
  • He says it was used in the Orlando shooting which is not the case.
  • He implies that the AR-15 "that can empty a 40-round clip in less than five seconds" which is stupid because the ARs use a 30 round magazine by default, I've never seen a 40 round magazine. It's also stupid because an AR uses a magazine, not a clip. The rate of fire he is claiming is 8 rounds per second which is basically humanly impossible for a semi auto unless you're bump firing it.
  • He claims the the noise produced was "humbling and deafening (even with ear protection)". If he thought it was that loud he was either wearing his ear protection incorrectly, or was using cotton balls taped to his forehead.
  • He claims "The recoil bruised my shoulder" which is insane because the recoil of an AR-15 is very minimal. You might have seen this hit the front page of Voat earlier demonstrating the recoil of an AR-15.
  • He says "The brass shell casings disoriented me as they flew past my face" which would be a valid complaint for someone operating it left handed but the picture in the article shows him holding it as a right handed person would and the brass would never fly in front of your face holding it like that.
  • "The smell of sulfur and destruction made me sick." First off there is no sulfur in modern smokeless gunpowder so that makes no sense. Secondly I have fired an AR-15 many times and I've never smelled "destruction" as a result, what does "destruction" actually smell like?
  • "The explosions — loud like a bomb — gave me a temporary case of PTSD." I really have no response to this. If his mental state is that fragile he should probably commit himself to an asylum.
  • "In fully automatic mode, it doesn’t take any imagination to see dozens of bodies falling in front of your barrel." AR-15s do not have a fully automatic mode. Fully automatic rifles have been banned in the US since 1985 and obtaining one requires getting past a bunch of federal red tape and a bunch of money. If I recall correctly you're going to end up spending at least $15,000 for one since they're not made anymore, and haven't been since 1985. This also incorrectly assumes that spray and pray is a valid tactic for something other than suppressive fire.
  • "Forty nine people can be gone in 60 seconds." I'm not familiar with the actual timeline of the Orlando events, but I highly doubt Mateen was able to murder all of his victims in 60 seconds. The fact that he was calling the police and posting about his actions on the internet during the massacre makes this claim highly suspect.
